title: A real sun, silver linings, meteor nights, and water that blends across biomes
intro: Your round 6 answers are built in. Every render this round uses the plain vanilla textures again: you found Faithful hurt the forest light, so it is back to vanilla unless a question is about textures. What changed since round 6: The sun is new. It is the true size now, a sharp disk that is darker toward its edge and whiter than the gold sky round it, turning orange only right at the horizon. Its glare is drawn over whatever stands in front of it, so trees and clouds cut it and thin cloud edges glow. The glare stays tight round the sun, so the sky is not washed out. Clouds get silver linings: their thin edges light up sharply toward the low sun, and their sunward sides get a warm rim. The forest rays are round 5's again, warm and well formed, with round 6's finer sampling. Dust in the air is bigger and a little denser, catches the light from more angles, and glints now and then. Nights rotate: the photographic Milky Way on almost half of them, deep clear on a third, and a new meteor shower on a quarter, lasting the whole night. Water now blends across biome borders by position, not only by where you stand. The game tints swamp water block by block, and the shader spreads that over about a dozen blocks, so a swamp fades into the ocean or river next to it. Fog and water colour that follow your own biome now fade over about ten seconds. The lake's near water should be less splotchy (the critic still sees patches: tell us what you see). River sparkle near you is tamed further, and swamp water has drifting algae mats and calm slicks. New: a Vibrance slider in the shader settings (0.15 by default), and light on blocks, which adds sunlight bounced off lit ground and a faint sheen at grazing light. The pack can now also read normal and specular maps from a texture pack (one question). Costs are per frame on High at 1440p, against the same view with shaders off. The budget is 3 ms and the dearest frame here is about 2.7 ms. Low and Potato stay in their budgets: Low at 1080p costs at most 0.80 ms (budget 0.9) and Potato at 720p at most 0.37 ms (budget 0.4). Frames marked 'round 5' or 'round 6' are earlier renders, shown for comparison; round 6 used Faithful. Clouds drift, so no two renders have quite the same sky. After the shader questions come the textures: our first own pack, QF Textures v0, against vanilla and Faithful on a new block wall, connected glass, the forest and golden hour; then a list of packs worth a look; then nine questions on Faithless, your inspiration pick. Faithless is all-rights-reserved, so those questions only link to its own pages and images; nothing of it is shown here. New on this page: you can attach your own images (screenshots, photos, other packs) to any answer with Add images.

scenes.name: A real sun
scenes.question: The ocean sunset, cropped tight round the sun and shown at four times the size. A is the new sun at its true size. At the game's field of view that is only about four pixels across, as a wide camera lens shows it. Its disk is sharp and darker toward the edge, and its glare is drawn over whatever is in front of it. B is the same sun 1.8 times larger, as a longer lens would show it, with a faint lens effect: a few dim ghosts and a soft six-point star. C is round 6's sun and clouds, with the same textures.
scenes.notePrompt: Which sun? Too small, too bright, the glare too much or too little? Keep the lens effect or not?

scenes.name: The lake at sunset: no more splotches
scenes.question: The lake in low light. Round 6's near water broke into torn patches. Some screen reflection rays turned downward off steep waves and mirrored the lake bed, and the sunset chop flipped facets between dark water and bright sky. Now those rays fall back to the sky, and the lake's chop is lower than the ocean's. Close up, the reflectance is averaged as the eye sees it. A is the new water, B round 6.

options.label: Round 6

scenes.name: Vibrance: a new slider
scenes.question: A Vibrance slider is now in the shader settings. It lifts muted colours (grass, sky, water) more than vivid ones, so wood, chests and gold do not turn neon. A is the default, 0.15. B is 0.35, and C is 0, which is round 6's colour.

options.label: 0.15 (default)
options.critic: Critic 7: A warm, good golden hour with the zenith still blue. Cloud tops are peach with a thin bright edge; the silver lining reads only on the smaller clouds. The horizon haze band is beige and flat.
Critic 6: Vibrance 0.35: the grass turns yellow-green and the lit patches push toward neon, which is too much. The clouds differ from A only because they drift.

options.label: 0 (round 6)
options.critic: Critic 7: Vibrance 0: duller, slightly grey grass. The frame loses some life against A's 0.15.

scenes.name: Rotating nights and a meteor shower
scenes.question: Nights now rotate: the Milky Way on almost half of them, deep clear on a third and a meteor shower on a quarter. A is the new meteor shower. It lasts all night: streaks from one point in the sky every few seconds, and now and then a bright one. At the burst rate used for A it costs about 0.4 ms more than a clear night; at the normal rate it should cost less. A was rendered at a burst rate so a still frame catches a few streaks; in play they come one at a time. B is the Milky Way night (round 6's render; its sky is unchanged). C is a deep clear night, which is what the rotation drew for this night.
scenes.notePrompt: Does the shower match the Milky Way's quality? Rate, length, brightness? Is the rotation mix right?

options.label: Meteor shower (new)
options.critic: Critic 7: Meteor night: two thin gold-white streaks low over the hill, crisp and believable, beside dark night clouds and a fine starfield. Rendered at a burst rate. It costs about 0.35 ms more than the deep clear night of the same view.

options.label: Milky Way (round 6 render)
options.critic: Critic 7: A real Milky Way: the photographed star clouds and dust lanes sit low in the sky under our stars and read as photographic, not drawn. Partly hidden by tonight's clouds, and faint, as it should be at this exposure.

options.label: Deep clear
options.critic: Critic 7: Deep clear (the rotation's pick for this night): a dense, fine starfield on navy-black, with dark night clouds whose thin edges take a little moonlight. No Milky Way tonight.

scenes.name: Normal and specular maps from a texture pack
scenes.question: The pack can now read the normal and specular maps a texture pack provides (the LabPBR format), so a block's surface relief and shine come from the pack. The test pack is QF Textures v0 from the texture work: vanilla, Faithful for a few blocks, and generated maps. A and C read the maps; B and D use the same pack with the maps ignored. A and B are the showcase wall (glass, ores, metal blocks), C and D golden hour in the showcase world, whose field has a dug pit (the dark patch). Known bug: with the maps on, a black smudge spreads over the dirt bank left of the glass in A.
scenes.notePrompt: Does the relief and shine read as real? Too strong anywhere?

options.label: Wall, maps on
options.critic: Critic 5: Maps on: the iron and gold blocks read more metallic (darker grey iron, richer gold), and the ores have a little relief. But a soft black blob spreads over the dirt bank left of the glass, which maps-off does not have: a PBR bug, probably bad normals or AO on dirt. The dark smear on the grass to the right is something in the world (it is there with shaders off too).

options.label: Wall, maps off
options.critic: Critic 6: Maps off, same pack: flatter metals and no black blob on the dirt. The showcase wall and the block sample row behind it are in view.

options.label: Golden hour, maps on
options.critic: Critic 5: The showcase world's golden view has a large black pit in the middle field that world-master does not have, so this pair is hard to judge. Maps on: the grass is a little more contrasty, otherwise much like maps off.

options.label: Golden hour, maps off

scenes.name: Faithless: the overall art style
scenes.question: Faithless is all-rights-reserved, so we only link to its official screenshots (they open on Modrinth) and would draw our own take; nothing is copied. 1. Every block redrawn in an early-Minecraft (Programmer Art) style, but each keeps its vanilla colour family. 2. Dark 1-pixel outlines and top-left light on every item icon. 3. Calm, low-noise terrain: grass, dirt, sand and snow in broad soft clusters, not speckle. 4. Neighbouring blocks clearly different in value and pattern, so no two look alike.

scenes.name: Faithless: GUI, menu and font
scenes.question: Faithless is all-rights-reserved, so we only link to its official screenshots (they open on Modrinth) and would draw our own take; nothing is copied. 23. Container screens in dark-wood frames with titled tabs and a small painted scene behind the slots (crafting bench, potion lab). 24. A brewing chart of every recipe beside the brewing stand (for us: a quest-book or NEI page). 25. Food tooltips with hunger and effects; an ornate boss bar; creative tabs as hanging banners. 26. A rounder, wider pixel font meant to be easier for dyslexic readers. 27. A title logo whose letters are made of blocks (waterfall, portal, creeper, ore).

scenes.name: Faithless: mobs, models and sound

Mobs redrawn in an early-Minecraft style: more human villagers, a more menacing dragon. 29. Breed variants for animals such as chickens (possible for us via random mobs). 30. Less-spidery spiders for arachnophobia (for us an optional add-on). 31. 3D models: braced fences, swinging lanterns, a 3D crafting table (not possible as a resource pack on 1.7.10; only for blocks we make ourselves). 32. scenes.name: Faithless: accessibility as a design rule
scenes.question: Faithless is all-rights-reserved, so we only link to its official screenshots (they open on Modrinth) and would draw our own take; nothing is copied. Its core rule: every block and item can be told apart by shape and pattern alone, so the pack works in full colourblindness (the author tested it with colourblind players). For us: a greyscale check in our texture build that flags blocks or items that look alike, plus the shape-coded ores, potions and books above. Also: no hole clusters (trypophobia), an optional spider skin (arachnophobia), a legible font.
